newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUCKLAND TO HOST WCC CLUB FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUCKLAND TO HOST WCC CLUB FINAL.

text.p: Auckland will host the million dollar final of Super League's world club challenge (WCC) on October 18, the Auckland Warriors club said on Thursday.
The Warriors have secured a management contract to run the game and the final should provide the financially battling club with an end-of-year cash injection.

The Warriors' impressive showing in the world event and solid, if unspectacular, attendance figures at their stadium have helped to persuade Super League to accept their bid, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
"We're rapt, and at that time of year there isn't a lot of other sport around," said chief executive Bill MacGowan.
"One thing in our favour was crowd support and we are still number two behind Brisbane, even though the side has struggled at times," he said.
The Sydney Football Stadium was the initial, tentative, venue.

But Super League's fears that they could be left with a small crowd -- a public relations disaster in their battle with the Australian Rugby League -- is believed to have been behind the move to take the game to Auckland.
Super League had apparently also considered venues such as Hong Kong.

Although the crowds for the first round of the WCC last month averaged about 12,500 in Australia compared to 6,750 in Britain and France, last weekend the British crowds averaged 7,805 while those down under had slipped back to 7,500.
The fact that 13,500 turned up in Auckland to watch the Warriors take on Bradford last Sunday helped support a switch to New Zealand for the final.
The Warriors are well placed to be one of the top two seeds in Australasian Pool A which means they would get a home quarterfinal against an English club.
If they finish third or fourth, they will have to travel to England.
Auckland will also get a home semifinal if they are seeded higher than their opponents.
